original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Preserve the exact fixed 48-step mixed_target_probe exponential interval through integer Horner evaluation and a closed rational remainder; measure the complete frozen PR4440 caller.
scope_change_reason: Takes ywz65 PR2552 Open next question 1 at a different retained interval engine, whose fixed stopping rule, exact rational outputs without dyadic rounding and geometric remainder need their own exact binding.
bottleneck_link: The separate rational exponential is a measured cost of complete query-controller replay. Exact arithmetic replacement can reduce review time without changing a mathematical decision.
stop_rule: Stop after the first exact complete-command improvement with five alternating fresh-process pairs and identical full outputs and exact call traces.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can the same source-specific integer evaluation help another exact moment engine with a different polynomial or remainder?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The gain and endpoint identity cannot be transferred from matching function names alone.
open_questions.first_step: Pin one engine, derive its exact endpoint formula and time its unchanged complete caller.
open_questions.blocked_by: No additional engine equivalence or performance result is supplied.
